title: Hebrews Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 5.

questions.question: In Hebrews 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Offering gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.correctAnswer: Offering gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.explanation: This is the first action mentioned in Hebrews 5:1, where it states that the high priest is ordained for men in things pertaining to God to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

questions.question: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, according to Hebrews 5?
questions.correctAnswer: The high priest
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:2 states that the high priest can have compassion on the ignorant and on those that are out of the way.

questions.question: What does the high priest offer for himself and the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices
questions.explanation: In Hebrews 5:3, it mentions that the high priest ought to offer for sins, both for the people and for himself.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5, who takes this honor of being a high priest?
options: No man takes it unto himself
questions.correctAnswer: No man takes it unto himself
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 states that no man takes this honour unto himself but he that is called of God.

questions.question: Who glorified not himself to be made a high priest?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:5 indicates that Christ did not glorify himself to be made a high priest.

questions.question: Who said to Christ, 'Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee'?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: This statement is made in Hebrews 5:5, where it indicates that it was God who said this to Christ.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the high priest being ordained for men?
options: To offer gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.correctAnswer: To offer gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:1 states that the high priest is ordained for men in things pertaining to God to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

questions.question: What does the high priest have compassion on?
questions.correctAnswer: The ignorant
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:2 specifically mentions that the high priest can have compassion on the ignorant.

questions.question: For whom does the high priest offer for sins?
questions.correctAnswer: Both himself and the people
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:3 states that the high priest ought to offer for sins for the people and also for himself.

questions.question: Who is compared to Aaron in terms of being called by God?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 compares the calling of Christ to that of Aaron, indicating that just as Aaron was called by God, so was Christ.

questions.question: Did Christ glorify himself to be made a high priest?
questions.correctAnswer: No
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:5 clearly states that Christ glorified not himself to be made a high priest.

questions.question: True or False: The high priest has compassion on those who are out of the way.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:2 states that the high priest can have compassion on those that are out of the way.

questions.question: True or False: No man can take the honor of high priest unto himself.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 states that no man taketh this honour unto himself but he that is called of God.

questions.question: True or False: Christ was called to be high priest by Aaron.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:5 indicates that Christ was called by God, not by Aaron.

questions.question: True or False: The high priest offers only for the people, not for himself.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:3 states that the high priest offers for both himself and the people.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5:6, after whose order is Jesus called a priest forever?
questions.correctAnswer: Melchisedec
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:6 states, 'Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 5:9 promise will happen if someone obeys Him, as commanded in Hebrews 5:8?
options: They will be exempt from suffering
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive eternal salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:8 commands obedience learned through suffering, and Hebrews 5:9 promises that by being made perfect, He became the author of eternal salvation to all who obey Him.

questions.question: What kind of prayers did Jesus offer during the days of His flesh, according to Hebrews 5:7?
options: Prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears
questions.correctAnswer: Prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 specifically states Jesus offered prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 5:10 relate to Hebrews 5:6 in describing Jesus' priesthood?
options: Both verses affirm Jesus is a high priest after the order of Melchisedec
One says Jesus is a priest after Aaron's order, the other says Melchisedec's
Hebrews 5:6 speaks of Jesus as a king, Hebrews 5:10 as a priest
Hebrews 5:10 denies the priesthood mentioned in Hebrews 5:6
questions.correctAnswer: Both verses affirm Jesus is a high priest after the order of Melchisedec
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:6 and 5:10 both confirm Jesus is called a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

questions.question: Why is Jesus able to have compassion on those who are ignorant and going astray, based on the context of Hebrews 5:7 and 5:2?
options: Because He experienced suffering and prayers in the flesh
Because He was sinless and perfect
Because He was a high priest by choice
questions.correctAnswer: Because He experienced suffering and prayers in the flesh
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 shows Jesus' suffering and prayers, and Hebrews 5:2 explains that priests can have compassion because they are also beset with infirmity.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 5:4 say about taking the honor of high priest?
options: No one takes it upon himself, but only when called by God
Anyone can take this honor if they desire
It is awarded by the people
questions.correctAnswer: No one takes it upon himself, but only when called by God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 states that no man takes this honor upon himself but is called by God, as was Aaron.

questions.question: How did Jesus learn obedience, according to Hebrews 5:8?
options: By the things which He suffered
questions.correctAnswer: By the things which He suffered
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:8 clearly states that although He was the Son, He learned obedience through suffering.

questions.question: What role does Hebrews 5:1 assign to every high priest taken from among men?
options: To offer gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.correctAnswer: To offer gifts and sacrifices for sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:1 explains that high priests are ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5:5, who glorified Christ to be made a high priest?
options: God who said, 'Thou art my Son, today have I begotten thee'
questions.correctAnswer: God who said, 'Thou art my Son, today have I begotten thee'
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:5 states Christ did not glorify Himself but was called by God with those words.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'being made perfect' in Hebrews 5:9 imply about Jesus' priestly role?
options: He completed His priestly mission and became the source of eternal salvation
He gained moral perfection through works
He was born perfect and needed no learning
He was perfected by the people’s approval
questions.correctAnswer: He completed His priestly mission and became the source of eternal salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:9 indicates that after being made perfect, He became the author of eternal salvation to those who obey Him.

questions.question: Why must high priests offer sacrifices for themselves as well as for the people, according to Hebrews 5:3?
options: Because they are subject to weakness and sin
Because they sin more than others
Because their sacrifices are more important
Because they want to set an example
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are subject to weakness and sin
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:3 explains that priests must offer for themselves due to their own infirmities.

questions.question: How does Jesus' experience of suffering and prayer in the flesh, described in Hebrews 5:7, offer practical encouragement to believers facing trials?
options: It shows that Jesus understands human weakness and intercedes for them
It suggests believers should avoid suffering
It implies that prayer is unnecessary during trials
It teaches that only priests can pray effectively
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that Jesus understands human weakness and intercedes for them
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 describes Jesus’ heartfelt prayers during suffering, indicating He empathizes and is able to save those who trust Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jesus being called a high priest 'after the order of Melchisedec' in practical Christian living?
options: It highlights His eternal and superior priesthood, offering believers lasting salvation
It means He served in the temple like Aaron
It limits His priesthood to a specific tribe
It shows He was a temporary priest
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights His eternal and superior priesthood, offering believers lasting salvation
questions.explanation: Both Hebrews 5:6 and 5:10 emphasize the order of Melchisedec to show Jesus’ eternal and perfect priesthood, assuring believers of eternal salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 5:4 teaches that a man can make himself a high priest without God's calling.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 explicitly states that no man takes this honor upon himself but is called by God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 5, Jesus did not experience human weakness or suffering.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 and 5:8 show that Jesus experienced suffering and learned obedience through it, indicating He shared in human weakness.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 5.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5:11, why is it difficult to speak about certain things to the audience?
options: They are wise beyond their years
questions.correctAnswer: They are dull of hearing
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:11 states it is hard to be uttered because the audience is 'dull of hearing', meaning slow to understand or unwilling to listen.

questions.question: In Hebrews 5:12, what are the audience said to need instead of being teachers?
options: To be taught again the first principles of the oracles of God
To be given more gifts and sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: To be taught again the first principles of the oracles of God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:12 explains that although they ought to be teachers, they need someone to teach them again the elementary truths of God's word.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Hebrews 5:12 to describe the spiritual maturity of the audience?
questions.correctAnswer: Milk and strong meat
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:12 contrasts milk (basic teaching) and strong meat (advanced teaching) to describe spiritual immaturity versus maturity.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5:13, who is described as 'unskilful in the word of righteousness'?
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone that uses milk
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:13 states that those who use milk are unskilful in the word of righteousness, meaning they are like infants in understanding.

questions.question: Hebrews 5:14 says strong meat belongs to those who are of what kind of age?
questions.correctAnswer: Full age
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:14 declares that strong meat belongs to those of 'full age', meaning mature believers who have exercised their senses.

questions.question: What is the result of exercise of the senses mentioned in Hebrews 5:14?
options: The ability to discern both good and evil
The ability to speak in tongues
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to discern both good and evil
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:14 teaches that those who practice discernment have their senses exercised to distinguish good and evil.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'teleios' used in Hebrews 5:14 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Mature or perfect
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'teleios' in Hebrews 5:14 means 'mature' or 'perfect', indicating spiritual completeness or full development.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in Hebrews 5:12-14 when contrasting 'milk' and 'strong meat'?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:12-14 uses metaphor by comparing basic and advanced teachings to milk and strong meat, respectively.

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure connected to priesthood is alluded to in Hebrews 5:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Melchisedec
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:6 refers to Christ being a priest 'after the order of Melchisedec', linking to Genesis 14:18 where Melchisedec is a priest-king.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Christ as high priest after the order of Melchisedec found in Hebrews 5:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 110:4
questions.explanation: Psalm 110:4 is cited in Hebrews 5:6 and 5:10 as the Old Testament basis for Christ's eternal priesthood after Melchisedec's order.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the statement in Hebrews 5:11 about the difficulty of teaching?
options: Christ being called high priest after Melchisedec's order
Christ offering prayers with strong crying and tears
The high priest offering gifts and sacrifices
The audience being dull of hearing
questions.correctAnswer: Christ offering prayers with strong crying and tears
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 describes Christ's prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears before Hebrews 5:11's teaching difficulty statement.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 5:8, what did Christ learn through suffering?
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:8 states that although Christ was the Son, he learned obedience through the things he suffered.

questions.question: In Hebrews 5:9, Christ is called the author of what?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternal salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:9 calls Christ the author of eternal salvation to all who obey him.

questions.question: Hebrews 5:12 uses the phrase 'first principles of the oracles of God.' What does this phrase imply about the nature of the teachings?
options: They are elementary or foundational truths
questions.correctAnswer: They are elementary or foundational truths
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:12 indicates the audience needs to be taught the 'first principles', meaning the basic foundational teachings of God's word.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 5:13 describes the spiritually immature as those who use milk.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:13 explicitly states that those who use milk are unskilful in the word of righteousness and are babes, indicating immaturity.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 5:5 teach about Christ's appointment as high priest?
options: Christ was glorified by Himself to become high priest
Christ was appointed high priest by divine calling as the Son of God
Christ was appointed by popular acclaim among men
Christ's priesthood was based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: Christ was appointed high priest by divine calling as the Son of God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:5 states that Christ did not glorify Himself to be made high priest, but was called by God, who said, 'Thou art my Son.' This shows the divine calling and appointment, not self-glorification or human merit.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's priesthood does Hebrews 5:6 teach?
options: Christ's priesthood is temporary and limited
Christ is a priest forever according to the order of Melchisedec
Christ's priesthood replaced the Aaronic priesthood but is inferior
Christ's priesthood is based on lineage from Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is a priest forever according to the order of Melchisedec
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:6 clearly states Christ is 'a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec,' affirming the eternal and superior nature of His priesthood.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's sanctification and obedience does Hebrews 5:8 teach?
options: Christ was disobedient in His suffering
Christ learned obedience through suffering despite being the Son
Christ did not suffer but was obedient by nature
Christ's obedience was irrelevant to His priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: Christ learned obedience through suffering despite being the Son
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:8 states that though Christ was the Son, He learned obedience through the things He suffered, emphasizing His experiential sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 5:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:7 describes Christ offering prayers and supplications to God who was able to save Him from death and heard Him because He feared, demonstrating God's mercy in hearing and responding.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 5:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternality
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:9 says Christ 'became the author of eternal salvation,' highlighting the eternal nature of the salvation He provides, thus reflecting God's attribute of eternality.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 5:1 prepare for the redemptive theme of priesthood and mediation in the New Testament?
options: By showing priests are divine beings
By establishing the human origin and divine calling of the high priest as mediator for men
By teaching that sacrifices are no longer necessary
By denying the need for mediation between God and man
questions.correctAnswer: By establishing the human origin and divine calling of the high priest as mediator for men
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:1 teaches that every high priest is taken from among men and ordained for men in things pertaining to God to offer gifts and sacrifices, setting the foundation for Christ's mediatorial priesthood.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 5:10 connect to the wider biblical narrative about priesthood?
options: It shows Christ's priesthood is according to Aaron's order
It reveals Christ's priesthood is a divine appointment after Melchisedec's order, fulfilling an eternal priesthood
It denies any continuity with the Old Testament priesthood
It teaches that all believers are high priests
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Christ's priesthood is a divine appointment after Melchisedec's order, fulfilling an eternal priesthood
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:10 confirms Christ was called by God to be a high priest after the order of Melchisedec, connecting with the eternal priesthood theme in Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 5:4 and 5:5 teach about the calling of the high priest?
options: The high priest takes the honor upon himself by human effort
No man takes the honor to be high priest unless called by God, as Christ was
The high priest's honor comes from popular acclaim alone
Christ self-designated His high priestly role
questions.correctAnswer: No man takes the honor to be high priest unless called by God, as Christ was
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:4 states no man taketh this honor unto himself but he that is called of God, and 5:5 shows Christ was so called, emphasizing divine appointment over human or popular claim.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 5:12 and 5:13 teach about spiritual maturity?
options: Believers should remain on milk since it is easier
Spiritual maturity involves moving from milk to strong meat and being skilled in righteousness
Milk and strong meat are irrelevant to spiritual growth
Only pastors need strong meat; all others remain on milk
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual maturity involves moving from milk to strong meat and being skilled in righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:12-13 describes the need to progress from milk to strong meat because milk is for the unskilful, showing that spiritual maturity requires growth in righteousness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 5:8 and 5:9 teach about Christ's perfection and salvation?
options: Christ's perfection was innate and unrelated to salvation
Christ became perfect through suffering and thereby became the author of eternal salvation for obedience
Christ's perfection was only moral, not salvific
Salvation is unrelated to Christ's obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Christ became perfect through suffering and thereby became the author of eternal salvation for obedience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:8 teaches Christ learned obedience through suffering, and 5:9 states He was made perfect and became the author of eternal salvation to those who obey Him, linking perfection, obedience, and salvation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 5:11-14 shows the author doubted the readers' salvation due to their dullness. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The readers are spiritually immature and need further teaching to grow
The readers have lost salvation due to dullness
The author condemns the readers as unbelievers
The readers are already perfect and need no further instruction
questions.correctAnswer: The readers are spiritually immature and need further teaching to grow
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:11-14 critiques the readers’ dullness of hearing and their need for milk instead of solid food, indicating immaturity, not a loss of salvation or condemnation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 5:2 teach about the high priest's role in relation to human weakness and sin?
options: The high priest is sinless and cannot sympathize with sinners
The high priest has compassion on the ignorant and those out of the way because he also is subject to weakness
The high priest is divine and above human infirmity
The high priest judges sinners without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: The high priest has compassion on the ignorant and those out of the way because he also is subject to weakness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:2 explains the high priest can have compassion on those ignorant and out of the way because he himself is surrounded by infirmity, showing solidarity with human frailty.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 5:9 specifically demonstrate in relation to salvation?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternality
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:9 states that Christ became the author of eternal salvation, emphasizing the eternal nature of God’s saving work.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 5:3 and 5:4 teach about the priest's responsibility for sin offerings?
options: The priest offers sacrifices only for others, not for himself
The priest must offer sacrifices both for the people and for himself, and must be called by God
Any man can take the honor of priesthood and offer sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The priest must offer sacrifices both for the people and for himself, and must be called by God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:3 says the priest must offer for sins both for the people and himself; 5:4 states no man takes the honor unto himself but he that is called of God, clarifying responsibilities and divine calling.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 5:14 illustrate the process of sanctification in the life of a believer?
options: Sanctification is instantaneous and does not require practice
Sanctification involves exercise and training of the senses to discern good and evil
Sanctification is unrelated to moral discernment
Only pastors can discern good and evil
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves exercise and training of the senses to discern good and evil
questions.explanation: Hebrews 5:14 speaks of those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil, highlighting the progressive and active nature of sanctification.
